def: Imagery, IMINT, and geospatial information used together.
Intelligence derived from interpretation of imagery.
Passive visible-light imaging.
Active radar imagery that works day and night in most weather.
A focused moving video feed used for tracking and observation.
Broad-area motion coverage with forensic look-back capability.
A sensor function that flags motion in a scene.
About 160 to 2,000 km altitude; best for high-resolution imagery.
About 2,000 to 35,786 km; commonly used for GPS / navigation.
About 35,786 km; fixed over one region for persistent coverage.
Used for highly inclined or polar coverage.
Intelligence from non-communications emitters such as radars, beacons, and jammers.
Intelligence from voice and data communications.
A system of systems using multiple radars, command and control, and interceptors.
The long-range Find layer in an IADS.
A precision radar that transitions detection into tracking.
The precision guidance layer used to support weapons engagement.
Radar and communications support that vectors interceptors onto a target.
Find - Fix - Track - Target - Engage - Assess; the sequence used to describe engagement progression.
The direct path required for most electromagnetic, optical, and IR collection.
Usually a shoulder-fired IR-guided missile system.
The heat spectrum used by many sensors and seekers.
A passive thermal imaging sensor used from aircraft or drones.
A passive fighter sensor used to detect and track aircraft heat signatures.
Satellite missile warning system that watches for launch plumes.
A seeker that builds a thermal picture of the target rather than chasing one hot point.
A simple IR seeker that locks onto the hottest point it can see.
IR countermeasure that creates a hotter decoy than the aircraft exhaust.
Radar countermeasure made of reflective material used against radar-guided threats.
Infrared Countermeasures - techniques or systems designed to defeat IR-guided weapons.
Military Information Support Operations - planned influence operations aimed at foreign audiences.
Military Deception - deception directed at adversary decision-makers.
Deliberately false information shared to deceive.
Inaccurate information shared without intent to deceive.
The hardware and infrastructure layer of the information environment.
The data, content, and signals layer of the information environment.
The beliefs, perceptions, and decision-making layer of the information environment.
A cyber attack that targets network integrity, availability, or confidentiality.
A threat that uses cyberspace as a delivery medium to create another effect, such as influence.
Reconnaissance, weaponization / delivery, exploitation / installation, command and control, actions on objectives.
Command and Control - the communications link used by an attacker or commander to direct actions.
Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures - the methods and patterns used by an actor.
The length of time an intrusion remains undetected inside a network or environment.
Priority Intelligence Requirement - the commander's top intelligence question.
Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance - the broader collection and analysis cycle.
Planning and Direction - the ISR stage where requirements become collection tasks.
Processing and Exploitation - the ISR stage where raw data is turned into usable intelligence.
Distributed Common Ground System - the primary processing and exploitation system in many ISR workflows.
Positioning, Navigation, and Timing - the core space-enabled navigation service.
Satellite Communications - communications relayed through space assets.
Anti-Satellite weapon - a weapon designed to damage or destroy a satellite.
Actions to deny, degrade, disrupt, destroy, or deceive space capabilities.
Counterspace that physically destroys or damages a space system.
Counterspace that disrupts, jams, dazzles, or degrades without physical destruction.
